notes: Independent answers produced without reading data/questions/** or content-cards. Only reviews/blind/F.json was consulted. Each code snippet was manually traced for shape/stride/mask/launch-config correctness. This file overwrites an earlier canary-partial containing 5 canary Qs.

answers.rationale: X: thousands of threads hit &out[0] => atomic-unit serialization. Y: block-local tree + 1 atomic per block => ~1/blockDim atomics. FP32 non-associativity permits minor differences.
Naive 3-kernel path stores S×S intermediate (S and P) in HBM per (B,H); ~2*S^2*2B. S=8192 => ~256MB per (B,H). Dominant cost, quadratic growth.

num_warps/num_stages are per-Config launch params (A). Autotuner keys off `key=` tuple, runs at first launch per key, caches best (D). B is wrong (autotuner runs at launch, not compile); C is wrong (searches only user-provided configs).

SMEM 32 banks, 4-byte wide. tile[32][32] FP32: bank(tile[i][j])=(i*32+j) mod 32 = j. W1 = tile[ty][tx] with warp varying tx (0..31): banks 0..31, conflict-free. R1 = tile[tx][ty] with warp varying tx and fixed ty per warp: all lanes hit bank ty => 32-way conflict. Fix: tile[32][33] pads so bank(i*33+j) = (i+j) mod 32, spreading across banks.
__syncthreads = block barrier; __syncwarp(mask) = warp barrier. On Volta+ ITS, explicit syncwarp often needed between shuffles that used to be implicitly convergent.

Warmup + synchronized event-timed inner loop is standard (C). Compare against reference with rtol/atol appropriate to dtype; torch.equal too strict (D). A false (no-warmup single-shot is unreliable), B false (autotune/JIT compile time must be excluded from steady-state).
make_block_ptr describes a [BM,BN] tile; boundary_check=(0,1) enables masking on both axes with zero fill; order=(1,0) declares axis 1 as fastest-varying (matches row-major).
CUDA Graph = captured DAG of ops instantiated to cudaGraphExec_t; repeated launch with much lower CPU overhead than per-op launches.

For stride=8 FP32, consecutive warp lanes read addresses stride*4=32B apart. 128B L1/L2 sector delivers 4 useful bytes/lane => effective BW ~ 1/stride of peak (~1/8). Global-memory coalescing/waste, not SMEM banking.
N is runtime scalar (same compiled kernel reused across N values); BLOCK: tl.constexpr => each distinct value triggers a new specialized PTX compilation.
64KB per module, dedicated constant cache, warp-uniform reads broadcast in one access.
FP16 has ~11 mantissa bits (eps ~9.77e-4). K=4096 accumulation with FP32 accum; observed rtol ~1e-3 is expected for FP16-input vs FP32-input reference. Likely correct.
cp.async introduced on sm_80; asynchronous GMEM->SMEM bypassing registers; completion via commit_group/wait_group; enables software pipelining.
A false — compiler emits predication when possible. B intra-warp divergence => cost sum of both paths. C blockIdx uniform across warp => no divergence. D predication computes both sides.

A correct (atomic_add necessary, out pre-zeroed by caller). B FP non-associativity across programs => non-determinism. C mask+other=0 preserves reduction identity for sum (0*anything=0). D false — atomic_add adds, not overwrites; non-zero init would corrupt result.

C tiling+online softmax avoids S×S materialization => O(S^2)->O(S) HBM traffic. D rescale factor exp(m_i-m_new) preserves exact algebra. A false (FlashAttention is numerically exact), B false (speedup from IO-awareness/tiling, not approx exp).

B FP16 precision insufficient for long K accumulation. C tl.dot lowers to mma.sync accepting FP16 operands with FP32 accumulator on Ampere+. A false (wmma/mma.sync support mixed precision on all Volta+). D false (FP32->FP16 cast loses precision when values are near FP16 quantum).
Per K-iter: 128*32*4 + 32*128*4 = 32768 B; FLOPs = 128*128*32*2 = 1,048,576. Intensity ~32 FLOPs/B, well above A100 FP32 balance (~13 F/B), so compute-bound.

GEMV is memory-bound; ~0.25 FLOPs/byte in FP32. Consecutive lanes read A[row*K+k] with k=lane, lane+32,... — consecutive lanes at consecutive addresses => coalesced within a warp. x is loaded redundantly per output row's warp.
Decode-phase: Q is 1 token, K/V are full S_kv per sequence => memory-bound; per-step HBM traffic scales linearly with S_kv.
sm_80 grid limits: x up to 2^31-1, y and z up to 65535; block up to 1024 threads. blockDim (32,32,1) = 1024 <= 1024 OK. gridDim (65535, 65535, 65535) all within limits => legal.
Fused kernel keeps row in registers/SMEM across mean/var/norm reductions; naive multi-pass reloads x from HBM => 2x traffic.
mma.sync is warp-cooperative: 32 lanes jointly execute one MMA, each holding operand/accumulator fragments in registers per HW-defined layout.
Regs cap: 65536/(96*256)=2.66 => 2 blocks. SMEM cap: 164/32=5.12 => 5. Thread cap: 2048/256=8. Block cap: 32. Binding = 2 blocks => 512 active threads => 25% occupancy.
Canonical online softmax: m=max(m_prev,m_new); s=s_prev*exp(m_prev-m)+s_new*exp(m_new-m). Exact algebra with new anchor.
For a max reduction, -inf is the identity so masked-out tail lanes do not bias the result. 0.0 would bias if all real values are negative.
Persistent kernel = fixed blocks (~SM count * blocks/SM) looping over global work queue via atomicAdd counter; amortizes launch overhead and tail load imbalance.
Missing __syncthreads between write smem[tid]=x[tid] and read smem[tid-1]. In multi-warp block, thread tid may read before thread tid-1 has written. Fix: __syncthreads() after the write.
Standard shuffle-down tree: 5 steps (log2(32)); lane 0 holds full warp sum; other lanes have partials. Consumers must read lane 0 or broadcast via shfl_sync.
'Local memory' in CUDA = per-thread private storage in device memory (backed by L1/L2/DRAM), not on-chip. Heavy spilling severely hurts performance.

With BLOCK=4096 FP32, each program holds ~16KB of x (plus intermediates + w) in registers/SRAM, constraining how many blocks can co-reside on an SM and thus occupancy. A false (other=0.0 zeroes tail => x*x=0 no bias). C fabricates 20% claim. D false (rsqrt.approx is not IEEE-strict).
Hillis-Steele: depth O(log N), work O(N log N). Blelloch: depth O(log N), work O(N) => work-efficient; access pattern more complex, often needs bank-conflict padding.

Softmax is invariant to constant subtraction (both numerator & denominator scale by e^{-x_max}); subtracting max prevents FP32 exp overflow at x~88.7. other=-inf is correct for max reduction identity.

C: same non-default stream = program order; different streams may run concurrently. D: EventRecord+StreamWaitEvent = cross-stream dependency without host block. A false (non-default streams do NOT block each other). B false (EventRecord is async on host).
Correct architectural history: Volta FP16, Turing INT8/INT4, Ampere added TF32/BF16/FP64, Hopper added FP8.
Read-only path via __ldg or const T* __restrict__ routes loads through read-only cache; useful for weight matrices etc. Kepler+.
pid_m=17: rows 544..575 (all <2048). pid_n=3: cols 384..511 (all <1024). Mask uniformly True; no lanes skipped.
pid=976: offsets 999_424..1_000_447; 576 valid, 448 OOB lanes masked out. tl.load with mask+other skips OOB loads; tl.store with mask skips OOB stores. No OOB access.
warpSize=32 fixed on NVIDIA; SM issues one instruction per warp; SIMT with per-lane predication for divergence.
nvcuda::wmma is a higher-level C++ template API compiling down to mma.sync + ldmatrix. Raw mma.sync gives finer control (used by CUTLASS).
